title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval
summary: Weekly POC check-in focused on quality regression checks across updated prompt sets. Reviewed latest scoring spreadsheet, discussed guardrails for PHI, and agreed to run a 10k-case benchmark on Redwood Dedicated. Action items: share updated prompt/score CSV, run dedicated infra eval, provide failure cases and privacy requirements.
action_items: Jordan Lee: Share prompt/score CSV and link to benchmark sheet by 2026-10-23
Priya Patel: Run 10k sample evaluation on dedicated infra (quantized + float) by 2026-10-28
Maya Torres: Provide anonymized failure cases and production error logs by 2026-10-25
Anika Rao: Confirm SOC2 scope and KMS requirements by 2026-10-26
Ethan Cole: Schedule 30-min infra planning call for dedicated nodes by 2026-10-27
next_steps: Send updated prompt set and scoring spreadsheet (Jordan)
Run 10k benchmark on Redwood Dedicated with v2 prompts (Priya)

transcript:
Meeting header: Date/Time: 2026-10-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Recorder: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE); Priya Patel (Redwood SE); Carlos Mendez (Redwood CSM); Maya Torres (Solstice Head of ML); Ethan Cole (Eng Mgr); Ravi Singh (Data Scientist); Anika Rao (Security)

Summary: quick recap at top - we compared v1 vs v2 prompts, noted regressions on two intent classes, talked about PHI guardrails, and agreed on a dedicated infra run to isolate latency/cost differences.

[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining 
we'll keep it to 45. quick agenda: results from the v2 prompt set, scoring highlights, guardrails, and next steps. Maya, you want to kick off with any updates on acceptance criteria?
[00:15] Maya Torres: Yeah, thanks Jordan. so from product we've been tracking two primary metrics: factual accuracy on triage suggestions and PII redaction rate. we're seeing overall accuracy up from v1 but there's a small regression on the "medication-change" intent where the model hallucinates a dosage. not super often but enough to fail our safety bar.
[01:05] Ravi Singh: yeah i pulled the logs 
about 1.4% of cases for med-change, the model invents a dosage number. attached in the sheet under "failure_cases_med_change".
[01:22] Priya Patel: ok that's helpful. we looked at that in the scoring spreadsheet 
thanks for uploading, Maya. on our side we ran the v2 prompt set with two scoring configs: precision-weighted and recall-weighted. precision-weighted reduced hallucinations by ~0.6% but dropped recall on multi-intent detection by ~1.2%.
[02:10] Ethan Cole: can you clarify the scoring function? like is that the thresholding on logits or post-filtering?
[02:18] Priya Patel: good question. it's a post-ranking score 
we score the generation with a classifier and then apply threshold T. for the run I shared it's T=0.78 for precision-weighted and T=0.66 for recall-weighted.
[02:42] Jordan Lee: quick note, we also put in a loose guardrail layer that checks for numeric fields that look like dosages, if an explicit dosage is generated and it's not in the patient record, we flag it. it's not perfect but reduces risk.
[03:05] Maya Torres: that's promising. is that the Redwood runtime guardrail or something you do post-processing?
[03:15] Priya Patel: it's a lightweight post-processing step in the response pipeline right now. we can push that into the runtime, though 
on Redwood dedicated we can run the filter as an inline step to minimize round trips.
[03:30] Anika Rao: from security, we need details on where those logs live 
we can't have PHI in those debug logs. do you have KMS and redaction workflow in place?
[03:42] Carlos Mendez: yes 
we're storing only hashed identifiers in the logs for the POC and the debug dumps are encrypted with customer-managed keys when requested. Jordan, I'll share the SOC two appendix after this call.
[04:00] Jordan Lee: noted, Carlos will share SOC two and KMS notes. (laughs) people keep saying SOC two these days.
[04:08] Maya Torres: also, we need an SLA on latency for triage responses. currently the hosted API is fine-ish but sometimes tails out around 800-900ms which hurts UX. our bar is 300-400ms p95.
[04:28] Priya Patel: right 
that's where dedicated vs hosted comes in. latency p95 on hosted with batching was around 720ms for the v2 prompts at the sample size we ran. on Redwood dedicate we expect lower p95 
we ran a small internal benchmark with quantized kernels and saw p95 ~340ms, but that depends on sequence length and KV cache hit rates.
[05:00] Ethan Cole: what about cost? dedicated committed nodes are a big ask for procurement.
[05:08] Jordan Lee: agreed. the tradeoff is predictable unit cost vs potentially higher per-token cost on hosted under bursty loads. for the POC we recommended a limited dedicated run 
say one week, 10k requests, to measure steady-state latency and unit cost.
[05:25] Maya Torres: sounds reasonable. can Redwood run the 10k on dedicated infra with the v2 prompts and both quantized and float configs? we want to see the quality delta as well.
[05:37] Priya Patel: yes we can. plan: run 10k with quantized (int8/awq) and float 16 and output per-case scores. we'll include latency, cost per 1k tokens, and the classifier score distributions.
[05:50] Jordan Lee: perfect. we'll annotate the sheet so you can filter by intent and failure type. link to the benchmark sheet is in the notes (drive.google.com/drive/benchmarks/solstice-poc) and prompt set v2 is at /redwood/prompt_sets/solstice-v2.csv
[06:12] Ravi Singh: quick question on guardrails: can the runtime do on-the-fly redaction if a PHI pattern is detected? we can't send PHI to customer logs.
[06:22] Priya Patel: yes 
runtime-level regex redaction and policy-based suppression is supported in Redwood private and dedicate; hosted by default supports configurable redaction but the debug dumps are sanitized. we should document the difference though 
good call.
[06:40] Maya Torres: ok let's ensure the PII cases are covered in the acceptance criteria, otherwise the benchmark is meaningless.
[06:50] Jordan Lee: agreed. we'll add PII redaction pass/fail columns to the sheet.
[07:00] Anika Rao: regarding compliance, do you support SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning? procurement will ask.
[07:08] Carlos Mendez: yes SAML and SCIM supported for enterprise customers; for POC we can do scoped access. I'll attach the integration notes in the follow-up.
[07:18] Ethan Cole: on the scoring, can you walk through an example where we lost recall 
like a real case?
[07:27] Priya Patel: sure 
here's an anonymized example: input had two intents: "refill" and "change-time"; the response prioritized refill and suppressed the second intent. in the precision-weighted run the classifier penalized the lower-confidence intent, so it got dropped. the multi-intent detector threshold needs tuning.
[08:00] Maya Torres: we can tolerate a small drop in recall for safety, but not for multi-intent detection 
our workflow relies on catching both intents.
[08:10] Jordan Lee: action item: Priya to tune multi-intent threshold and re-run a 2k sample to demonstrate improved recall without increasing hallucinations.
[08:22] Priya Patel: will do. also, one note 
we pushed a guardrail that strips numeric dosage if not matched in patient record, but will tag it for human review in the UI. that's in the demo branch if you want to see it.
[09:00] Maya Torres: good. for acceptance criteria: 1) PII redaction pass rate >= 99.9% on test set, 2) triage factual accuracy >= 94% across intents, and 3) multi-intent recall >= 92%. are those numbers acceptable?
[09:20] Ethan Cole: need to confirm with product, but ballpark yes.
[09:28] Jordan Lee: ok we'll use those as provisional targets.
[09:33] Priya Patel: on rollout, once we clear the benchmark we'll recommend a canary: route 5% traffic to the Redwood endpoint with enhanced logging (sanitized) for two weeks, then ramp. Redwood supports canary policies and automatic fallback to hosted model variants on regressions.
[09:55] Maya Torres: fallback is important 
how fast is the rollback?
[10:03] Jordan Lee: rollback is immediate at the routing level 
traffic can be re-routed to the previous model version in under a minute via the console or API.
[10:12] Anika Rao: can you produce an audit log of who performed the rollout? we need that for compliance.
[10:18] Carlos Mendez: yes audit logs are available in the private control plane and we can stream them to your SIEM via syslog or S3 export.
[10:28] Maya Torres: great. on procurement, what docs do you need from us to start a dedicated trial?
[10:35] Jordan Lee: typically an MOU is enough for a short dedicated trial, plus network access for the VPC peering if you want private connectivity. we'll also need a contact for certs and KMS if you want customer-managed keys.
[10:50] Ethan Cole: procurement will want numbers on expected spend. can you provide an estimate for a week-long dedicated run of 10k requests?
[10:58] Jordan Lee: yes 
Priya i'll follow up with the cost estimate, including quantized vs float differences. we'll put ranges in the sheet.
[11:08] Priya Patel: noted. I'll include cost per 1k tokens for both runs and a rough total.
[11:18] Ravi Singh: small nit: some of the prompts in v2 are longer, which inflates token counts. should we standardize prompt length to control for cost variance?
[11:28] Maya Torres: yes we should normalize prompt templates; I'll have a doc with final templates by Friday.
[11:36] Jordan Lee: action item: have Maya share final prompt template; we'll lock the prompt set and then run the benchmark.
[11:44] Maya Torres: will do.
[11:48] Jordan Lee: any other blockers?
[11:52] Anika Rao: just to reiterate, send SOC two appendix and confirm that debug logs will be encrypted and sanitized 
cannot have raw PHI.
[12:02] Carlos Mendez: will send after call.
[12:08] Jordan Lee: ok quick recap 
Priya runs 10k on dedicated with quant+float, includes latency and classifier scores; Jordan/Carlos share SOC2/KMS appendix and prompt/score sheet; Maya provides failure cases and final prompt templates; Anika to confirm compliance constraints. Follow-up call the week of 2026-11-02 to review results.
[12:30] Maya Torres: thanks everyone, appreciate the quick sync.
[12:35] Jordan Lee: thanks 
will send notes and links shortly. bye.

References / Links mentioned: prompt set v2: /redwood/prompt_sets/solstice-v2.csv ; benchmark sheet: https://drive.google.com/drive/benchmarks/solstice-poc ; SOC2 appendix: will be shared by Carlos (link to be provided)

End of transcript.
